entries.contrast: ✗ Mother-in-laws is the commonest error. The possessive, however, does go at the end: my mother-in-law's house. All the in-law terms follow: fathers-in-law, brothers-in-law, sisters-in-law, sons-in-law, daughters-in-law.

entries.agreement: plural verb — his brothers-in-law both work there
entries.contrast: ✗ Brother-in-laws is wrong. English uses one term where Russian distinguishes several relationships — the brother of your spouse and the husband of your sister are both brother-in-law.

entries.contrast: ✗ Passerbys is wrong. The -s goes on passer, the noun, not on by, which is an adverb.

entries.variants: attorneys general in legal and formal writing; attorney generals is common in American journalism
entries.contrast: General here is an adjective, not the military rank — the phrase means 'general attorney' in French word order. The traditional plural puts the -s on attorney. Both forms now appear in edited American prose.
